content: Nystatin ointment is an antifungal, polyene antibiotic approved by the FDA for treating cutaneous or mucocutaneous fungal infections caused by Candida albicans and other Candida species. Common adverse reactions include irritation at the site of topical application. For adults, Nystatin ointment is indicated for the treatment of fungal infections of the skin or mucous membranes caused by Candida species. The ointment should be applied liberally to the affected areas twice daily or as directed until complete healing occurs. In cases of candidiasis involving intertriginous areas, Nystatin cream is generally preferred over the ointment. For very moist lesions, Nystatin topical powder is considered the most effective treatment. This preparation does not stain the skin or mucous membranes and offers a simple and convenient method of treatment. There is limited information regarding off-label uses of Nystatin ointment in adults, both guideline-supported and non-guideline-supported. For pediatric patients, there is limited information available regarding FDA-labeled indications, dosages, and off-label uses of Nystatin ointment. Nystatin ointment is contraindicated in patients with a known hypersensitivity to any of its components. If a hypersensitivity reaction occurs, the medication should be discontinued immediately, and appropriate measures should be taken. This preparation is not intended for ophthalmic use. Nystatin is virtually non-toxic and non-sensitizing, making it well-tolerated across all age groups, including debilitated infants, even with prolonged administration. If irritation occurs at the site of topical application, the medication should be discontinued. There is limited information available regarding postmarketing experience, drug interactions, and specific population use (e.g., pregnancy, labor and delivery, nursing mothers, pediatric, geriatric, gender, race, renal impairment, hepatic impairment, immunocompromised patients). Nystatin is an antifungal antibiotic that exhibits fungistatic and fungicidal activity in vitro against a wide range of yeasts and yeast-like fungi. Its mechanism of action likely involves binding to sterols in the fungal cell membrane, altering membrane permeability, and causing leakage of intracellular components. It is derived from Streptomyces noursei and is the first well-tolerated antifungal antibiotic with reliable efficacy for treating cutaneous, oral, and intestinal infections caused by Candida albicans and other Candida species. It has no significant activity against bacteria. Nystatin provides specific therapy for all localized forms of candidiasis. Symptomatic relief is often rapid, occurring within 24 to 72 hours after initiating treatment. Clinical and mycological cures are achieved in most cases of localized candidiasis. Nystatin ointment is supplied as a yellow ointment containing 100,000 USP Nystatin units per gram in a polyethylene and mineral oil base. It is available in 15-gram and 30-gram tubes. The product should be stored at controlled room temperature (15°–30°C or 59°–86°F). Patients should be advised to keep this and all medications out of the reach of children. The ointment is for topical use only and is not intended for ophthalmic use. There is no established interaction between alcohol and Nystatin ointment, but patients should consult their healthcare provider regarding alcohol use while on this medication.
